title: Dyspeptic symptom development after discontinuation of a proton pump inhibitor: a double-blind placebo-controlled trial
authors: Niklasson A, Lindström L, Simrén M, Lindberg G, Björnsson E
followUp: 28 days of treatment and 6 weeks after
population: Healthy Helicobacter pylori-negative volunteers (24 women) randomised to pantoprazole 40 mg or placebo once daily for 28 days
funder: Not read: the publisher page required payment and the article is not in PubMed Central.
result: In the first week after stopping, 11 of 25 (44%) on pantoprazole developed dyspepsia against 2 of 23 (9%) on placebo (P < 0.01); mean Glasgow dyspepsia score 5.7 against 0.74 in week 1 and 1.6 against 0 in week 2, with no significant difference in week 3. Symptom scores in week 1 correlated with basal and meal-stimulated gastrin at the end of treatment.
